notes: v270 — CLOSE-END-FUTURE-GUARD + TRAVEL-MISSING-ON-TRACKER-CLOSE (owner, Mon Oct 26, 2026 17:07 MDT, his screenshot of the End shift sheet: closing at 5:06 PM he set the end to the foreman ticket's finish, 6:00 PM, and the app popped "6:00 PM hasn't happened yet — it's 5:06 PM now. End the shift at 5:06 PM instead?" His words: "That shouldn't be a limitation... Because I wanna stop it 6 pm as per the ticket!"). Pay follows the FOREMAN TICKET — its finish is the truth and is routinely ahead of the moment he performs the close. FIX 1 (js/app.js trackerSaveEnd): the v249 confirm-to-now substitution is DELETED — a chosen end later than now on the same day books exactly as entered, no dialog, no swap; the close books the session to the entered end (session seconds and endedAt computed to it) through the unchanged review -> Confirm path. Kept sanities (not asked to be removed): the end is still a time-of-day on the session's start date with the overnight roll for an on-the-clock-earlier end, the zero-second refusal ("not after the start"), and the >12 h shift-length confirm. The session stays closed: stopSessionAt's stop stamps through the v265 machinery as any close does (tracker idle in the store, the native record cleared by the plugin stop path, rev-stamped syncs); nothing in the future end re-opens it — proven across a simulated relaunch collect before AND after the booked end passes, and against a cloud pull carrying the stale RUNNING session. FIX 2 (TRAVEL-MISSING-ON-TRACKER-CLOSE, same incident: he tapped OK and the day booked as a bare "Auto from tracker" $264.69 = 9.13h x $29 with NO travel hour): on a day with an active dispatch (the app's own day resolution, autostartDispatchFor — the v263 miles-gate test — read against the session's start day), a tracker close now composes the day like a dispatch close: stopSessionAt stamps the session with his Preferences travel bonus (new closeTravelFor helper in js/app.js), the close review prices the same composition (endCloseSummary), and Revenue's onSession (modules/revenue.js) books foreman (session) hours + travel = paid hours at his rate with the split fields stored (foremanHours / travelHours / travelInIncome), priced into `hours` + `amount` so a later rate edit re-derives the same total. No dispatch that day — no travel invented; the v38 rule stands for unstamped sessions. The v241 one-close law is untouched: a completion entry for the day still silences the tracker entry entirely (no double travel). Hourly books only (travel is an hours concept), mirroring dspCompletionPlan's driver branch — the tracker close is by construction the driver who drove.
